tried: The Dropbox PDF link on the report page refuses the fetch tool (robots), so it was opened in the desktop app's browser with raw=1 (served inline from dl.dropboxusercontent.com), fetched in-page and parsed with pdf.js: 68 pages, created 17 Mar 2026 in Adobe InDesign. Its text layer does not extract (subset fonts without usable Unicode maps), so every page was rendered to a canvas and read with Tesseract OCR in the browser; nothing was saved to disk.

OCR reads body text well but misreads some large infographic numerals (the Coast page's headline came back as '2 0'); the counts were therefore taken from the Infogram chart data behind the web edition (window.infographicData of each embed, which holds the 2015-2025 series and the 10-year average) and checked against the PDF's headline figures and captions, which agree on every page used.

The report prints no formal definition of a preventable drowning: searched all 68 OCR pages for 'preventable' (pp. 4 and 6 only) and 'non-preventable', 'DrownBase' and 'glossary'; the glossary (pp. 63-67) defines categories, not inclusion.
notes: The four placeholder rows can now carry printed counts: Pools 3 (p. 41), Home 3 (p. 42), Underwater 6 (p. 31), Other recreation 6 (p. 33); the all-sex Coast count is 29 (p. 35 text; chart), of which 27 were men, so the ledger's inference of 'about 29' is confirmed by the source. A reviewer may note, without the lab summing anything, that the seven environment values the report prints (29, 14, 17, 3, 9, 3, 3) and the six activity values (15, 17, 10, 6, 24, 6) are each consistent with the total of 78 the report prints. The chart data also gives the 2015-2025 series and the 10-year averages for every environment and activity (recorded in the corrections' scope fields), which the web edition shows only as graphics. The 'definition of preventable drowning' the task asked for does not exist in the PDF as a definition; the closest sentence is on p. 6 and is recorded as a definition row. Page numbers are the report's printed numbers, which equal the PDF page index. PDF text was obtained by OCR of rendered pages, so quotes from it were checked against the page image text; the chart figures come from the publisher's own data arrays, not OCR.
